basis: Migraine with motor aura is neurologic; visual and auditory aura do not establish direct eye or ear damage.
Breaks in retinal Bruch membrane define the ocular lesion; associated systemic disorders are separate conditions.
Acute fallopian tube infection, usually ascending bacterial infection; reproductive anatomy has no organ axis.
Developmental disability, ataxia and seizures define a neurologic disorder; nystagmus and opsoclonus do not establish intrinsic eye damage.
Lysosomal ganglioside storage causes progressive neuronal dysfunction in most patients; visceral and skeletal involvement varies across subtypes.
Inherited cerebral cleft malformation; broader COL4A1-associated organ findings are not established as common in familial schizencephaly.
Immune-mediated intestinal inflammatory disease; extraintestinal diseases are not established as common intrinsic manifestations of this subtype.
Renal tubular fibrosis defines disease; cholestasis and intellectual disability each occur in 2/6 (~33%); hypertension is secondary to kidney failure.
Metaphyseal sclerosis and skeletal dysplasia define disease; developmental delay has a single-patient annotation, while intellectual disability and seizures are occasional.
Achalasia, microcephaly and intellectual disability define the syndrome; dermatoglyphic and facial differences do not establish additional organ damage.
Glomerulosclerosis and tubulointerstitial fibrosis directly damage the kidneys.
Eye and skin anomalies define syndrome; skeletal deformity/muscle atrophy and thyroid gland abnormalities are frequent (30-79%); anorexia alone adds no GI axis.
Familial infantile epilepsy affects cerebral neuronal function; no common direct damage to other organ axes is established.
Developmental delay and intellectual disability commonly characterize pathogenic partial X duplications; other organ abnormalities vary with the duplicated segment.
Disordered zinc absorption, transport or metabolism defines this umbrella; skin, renal and neurologic damage are subtype-dependent.
Autoimmune inflammation directly damages blood vessels; additional organ involvement depends on the vasculitis subtype.
Sensory Guillain-Barre variant is an immune-mediated peripheral neuropathy.
Teratoma originates in the stomach; its heterogeneous tissue composition does not imply other organ involvement.
A pervasive neurodevelopmental disorder with developmental and social impairment; neurodevelopmental conditions belong to the neurologic axis.
PDE6B-associated rod-cone retinal degeneration; cataract remains within the ocular axis.
Malignant tumour originates in the small intestine; fibroblastic histology does not establish locomotor-system involvement.
Developmental malformation of cochlear and vestibular ear structures.
Fungal infection directly involves an intervertebral disc.
CHMP2B-associated cortical and motor-neuron degeneration; denervation weakness does not establish a separate primary muscle disorder.
Parametrium is reproductive supporting tissue outside the axes; its connective tissue is not part of the locomotor system.
